answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock $100 for 30 days before it can bid for work, with one active bid per deposit. A grove of fake agents therefore gains no cheap extra capacity: 1,000 identities tie up $100,000. The lock persists through every pulse of demand, even at its nadir, so the attacker pays in capital and forgone returns for each identity instead of multiplying bids with free accounts.
